seed.title: ABCD SYNDROME

records.label: Proband (14th child)

phenotypes.text: black lock at right temporo-occipital region
total absence of neurocytes and nerve fibers in the small intestine

quotes: We report on a macrosomic newborn girl with albinism, a black lock at the right temporo-occipital region, and retinal depigmentation. Bilateral deafness was confirmed by brainstem auditory-evoked potentials.

Biopsy showed aganglionosis of the large intestine, and total absence of neurocytes and nerve fibers in the small intestine, indicating a total lack of sympathetic and parasympathetic innervation. The infant died of intestinal dysfunction at 5 weeks.
She was the 14th child of consanguineous Kurdish parents.

records.label: Four affected sibs of the proband
records.age_last: died a few days after birth
quotes: Four sibs of our patient had the same syndrome and died a few days after birth. The other 9 sibs are well, with an unremarkable phenotype.

records.label: Index patient of the ABCD syndrome family
quotes: we screened DNA of the index patient of the ABCD syndrome family for mutations in the endothelin B receptor (EDNRB) gene
A homozygous nonsense mutation in exon 3 (R201X) of the EDNRB gene was found.

notes.statement: Verheij et al. (2002) described ABCD syndrome as an autosomal recessive syndrome characterized by albinism, black lock, cell migration disorder of the neurocytes of the gut (Hirschsprung disease), and deafness.
quotes: ABCD syndrome is an autosomal recessive syndrome characterized by albinism, black lock, cell migration disorder of the neurocytes of the gut (Hirschsprung disease [HSCR]), and deafness.

notes.statement: Because the phenotype overlaps with Shah-Waardenburg syndrome and they found a homozygous EDNRB mutation, Verheij et al. (2002) suggested that ABCD syndrome is not a separate entity but an expression of Shah-Waardenburg syndrome.
quotes: This phenotype clearly overlaps with the features of the Shah-Waardenburg syndrome, comprising sensorineural deafness; hypopigmentation of skin, hair, and irides; and HSCR.
We therefore suggest that ABCD syndrome is not a separate entity, but an expression of Shah-Waardenburg syndrome.

notes.statement: Gross et al. (1995) proposed autosomal recessive inheritance for ABCD syndrome. Their evidence was that the parents were consanguineous and that 5 of their 14 children were affected.
quotes: She was the 14th child of consanguineous Kurdish parents.
It represents a new neural crest syndrome with autosomal-recessive inheritance.

notes.statement: Gross et al. (1995) described ABCD syndrome as a new neural crest syndrome. Its features are albinism, a black lock, deafness, and a complete lack of neural innervation of the gut.
quotes: A syndrome of albinism, black lock, deafness, and a total lack of intestinal neural innervation has not yet been reported. It represents a new neural crest syndrome with autosomal-recessive inheritance.
